findings.title: Ungrouped OR fragments break AND composition and can skip authorization
findings.body: Team and org authorization SQL is an OR of two branches with no surrounding parenthesis group: ("teamId" = … AND "isTeamBooking" = true) OR ("userId" = ANY(…) AND "isTeamBooking" = false), built at the reduce in buildOrgAuthorizationCondition (line 173) and buildTeamAuthorizationCondition (line 204). The event-type filter is the same shape: ("eventTypeId" = $id) OR ("eventParentId" = $id) at line 106, also returned without an outer group when it is the only filter. getBaseConditions wraps each side only when both auth and filters are present (line 73). With no service filters it returns the bare authorization fragment here. That is the common insights path: this service only filters eventTypeId and memberUserId, and findMany (which AND-merged arbitrary caller where-clauses inside Prisma, so grouping was safe) was removed. Callers must add the time window themselves. WHERE ${getBaseConditions()} AND "startTime" >= $from AND "status" = 'accepted' is parsed as (team branch) OR (personal branch AND startTime >= $from AND status = 'accepted') because AND binds tighter than OR. Every team booking for that team is included regardless of date or status, so team/org insights over-count and ignore caller predicates. A second composition, WHERE ${getAuthorizationConditions()} AND ${getFilterConditions()}, is the obvious translation of the old findMany AND and is also wrong: it parses as (auth AND eventTypeId = $id) OR eventParentId = $id, so any booking whose eventParentId matches is returned even when it fails the org/team/user authorization predicate. That leaks rows for child/managed event types outside the caller's scope. Wrap every returned fragment, including the final OR and this no-filter return, in parentheses (Prisma.sql`(${fragment})`) before it is embedded. The new tests expect the unparenthesized text, so they lock the unsafe shape in.

findings.title: Team/org SQL is never executed; toEqual does not match nested Prisma.sql
findings.body: The team-scope assertion here, the org-scope assertion around line 332, and the combined-filter assertion around line 429 compare getAuthorizationConditions/getFilterConditions to a single flat Prisma.sql template via toEqual. Those service methods build the predicate with Array.reduce, so the returned Prisma.Sql values array holds nested Sql fragments; flattening happens only when a query is executed, not in the constructor. vitest deep-equality compares that structure, not rendered SQL, so these three tests fail even when the SQL text matches. NOTHING, user-scope, and single-filter cases are flat templates and can pass, which hides the failure mode. The only query actually sent to the database is the user-scope getBaseConditions case (line 481), which is a pure AND and does not use OR or ANY(array). A passing run therefore does not check team/org authorization, array binding for ANY(${ids}), or the operator-precedence bug when these fragments are AND-ed with a date or status predicate. Execute the team and org fragments with $queryRaw (including an extra AND predicate) and assert both included and excluded rows.
